newsitem.title: UK: NatWest up again on continued bid talk.
newsitem.headline: NatWest up again on continued bid talk.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc rose in early trade on Tuesday as bid speculation continued to swirl around the group, dealers said.
In a mostly weak bank sector, NatWest was up 6p at 789-1/2 by 0752 GMT in volume of 701,724 shares.
On Monday the stock rose 37p as press reports said the bank could be a target for Barclays Plc.

The influential Financial Times Lex column said talk of a Barclays bid for NatWest could be "wide of the mark" but that NatWest was "definitely in play and the profits from acquiring it are potentially mouth-watering."
The Lex report said NatWest's break-up value could be 3 billion stg higher than its current market capitalisation and that NatWest would not be well-placed to resist a takeover approach.
Analysts at brokerages including ABN AMRO Hoare Govett were positive on NatWest shares. Peter Toeman at Hoare said he had repeated his positive stance on the stock.
